slowest_experiments.label: Exp 219: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Sequential model loading — Qwen then Gemma loaded into a single GPU, each requiring full VRAM allocation before the previous was freed. Second RTX 3090 sat idle throughout. No DualGPURunner wired into conductor at this point in the milestone sequence.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 308: JEPA fast-path gate integration (tests failing checkpoint)
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Interrupted conductor run left test suite in a failing state. Recovery required reading stale partial results, identifying which tests were new vs pre-existing failures, re-running the full suite, and re-committing — adding at least 30-40 minutes of diagnostic overhead on top of the experiment itself. No partial-result fast-path existed.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 184: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: 3B-parameter model (4x larger than 0.8B baseline) required proportionally more VRAM and per-token inference time. The verify-repair loop ran 3 forward passes per question (verify + repair + re-verify) on a single GPU, making the cost multiplicative. No prompt-side batching to amortize model loading latency.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 221: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Full typed IR generation pipeline ran sequentially across prompt variants with no batching. Constraint evaluation was single-threaded. Typed IR prompts are longer than GSM8K prompts, increasing per-call token cost and reducing effective throughput.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 425: Conductor timeout watchdog — RETRO-003 (17+ milestone carry)
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Implementing a timeout watchdog deferred for 17+ milestones required writing ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog from scratch, adding 35 tests, updating specs, and integrating into experiment_template.py. Wall time includes reading all prior RETRO-003 history to understand the full scope. The meta-irony: this experiment was itself at risk of needing a timeout.

bottlenecks_identified: GPU 1 zombie VRAM leak (RETRO-025, open at milestone end): device_map='auto' allocates VRAM on GPU 1 for layer offloading without placing any compute there. GPU 1 at 76% VRAM (18688MB) with 0% utilization during single-model experiments. Fix implemented in Exp 438 but not live-verified — estimated 1786MB wasted continuously across the milestone.

Repeated re-verification of already-implemented code: Exp 447 (KAEMEnergy) was verified three times in separate sessions (conductor, human, human again) without any code changes between runs. This pattern appeared at least 4 times during the milestone (Exps 439, 444, 446, 447). Each re-verification cost 8-20 minutes of reading + test re-running with no new output.

Sequential model loading on dual-GPU hardware: Exp 219 (117 min) and all dual-model benchmarks loaded models one at a time onto GPU 0, leaving GPU 1 idle during inference. DualGPURunner was discussed but not wired into the conductor. At 16 min/exp average, sequential loading on paired models adds approximately 8 min overhead per dual-model experiment.

RETRO-003 (conductor timeout) carried 17+ milestones before implementation at Exp 425: runaway experiments (e.g., PID 3509070, 144 min at 82C) were not killed automatically. Over the milestone, an estimated 3-5 runaway experiments x 45 min average overshoot = 135-225 minutes of wasted GPU time and thermal stress.

Conductor checkpoint interruptions with no fast-path recovery: Exp 308 (105 min) shows a failing-test checkpoint requiring full manual triage. When the conductor is interrupted mid-experiment, no structured partial-result handoff exists. The next session must re-read all context, identify what was and was not committed, and re-run the full test suite — adding 30-40 min per incident.

Preflight-blocked experiments counted as 'completed': many experiments in the 311 total reached status=scaffolding_only or LIVE RUN PENDING, meaning the harness was built but no live GPU result was produced. Conservative estimate: 40-60% of experiments produced real data vs scaffolding, inflating experiment count without advancing research outcomes.

Pre-flight test suite overhead on doc-only turns: the full 3900+ test suite ran after every commit including changelog and ops doc updates. At 60-90s per run and approximately 80 doc-only commits in a 311-experiment milestone, this adds 80-120 minutes of pure test overhead with no code change being validated.

No parallelism in conductor: experiments ran strictly serially. Multi-GPU hardware sat idle between experiment teardown and the next experiment's startup. Inter-experiment gap (cleanup + commit + context load) estimated at 2-4 min x 311 experiments = 10-21 hours of potential parallel opportunity.

RETRO-022 (env propagation) carried until Exp 413: CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE was never exported into conductor subprocesses, causing 6+ consecutive milestones of blocked live experiments. Earlier detection via a simple conductor health check at session start would have caught this on milestone 1.

Doc reconciliation passes scheduled as full separate turns: updating ops/status.md, _bmad/traceability.md, and conductor-log.md in separate turns after each experiment added 2-5 min per experiment in context-loading overhead.
improvements_suggested: Implement conductor session health check at startup: before the first experiment of any session, verify CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE propagates to subprocesses (one-line check). If it fails, self-inject and log WARNING. This alone would have prevented the RETRO-022 6-milestone block. Estimated savings: 60-90 min per milestone where env propagation is broken.

Wire DualGPURunner into experiment_template.py for all dual-model experiments: assign model A to cuda:0 and model B to cuda:1 using explicit device_map={'': 'cuda:N'} (the Exp 438 strategy). Run both models in parallel threads during inference phases. Estimated throughput improvement on dual-model benchmarks: 1.5-1.8x.

Add automatic GPU memory cleanup between experiments: after each experiment teardown, call torch.cuda.empty_cache() and verify nvidia-smi shows <200MB residual on each GPU before starting the next experiment. This prevents VRAM accumulation that degrades subsequent experiments.

Add experiment-state deduplication check to conductor: before scheduling an experiment, check if its result JSON already exists and honest_verdict is not 'partial' or 'blocked'. If results are already present and healthy, skip re-implementation. This would prevent the Exp 447 triple-re-verification pattern.

Create a 'doc-only' commit classifier: if the diff touches only README.md, docs/, ops/*.md, or _bmad/*.md, skip the full 3900-test suite and run only ruff + mypy (5-10s total). This eliminates 80-120 min of unnecessary test overhead per milestone.

Add per-experiment partial-result handoff protocol: when the conductor is interrupted (SIGTERM, timeout, or exception), automatically serialize the partial ExperimentTemplate state to results/experiment_NNN_partial.json before exit. The next session can fast-path to resume rather than triage from scratch. Estimated recovery time reduction: 30-40 min per interrupted experiment.

Enforce inference batching in all benchmark harnesses: batch_size=8 for GSM8K (50 questions), batch_size=4 for HumanEval (longer prompts). A single batched forward pass amortizes model loading and tokenization overhead. Expected 3-5x reduction in per-question inference latency at current GPU utilization levels.

Add GPU thermal throttle gate: if any GPU exceeds 80C, pause the conductor and log a RETRO item. Do not start the next experiment until temperature drops to 70C. This prevents thermal damage (RTX 3090 observed at 82C during runaway experiment) and preserves hardware for Phase 2 FPGA work.

Unify end-of-experiment doc update into a single atomic write per experiment: changelog.md + ops/status.md + conductor-log.md + traceability.md should all be updated together rather than in separate turns. Estimated savings: 2-4 min x 311 experiments = 10-21 hours across the milestone.

Schedule live GPU experiments in dedicated 'live' sessions and scaffolding experiments in 'dry' sessions: do not mix blocked scaffolding and live inference in the same conductor session. The live session can assume CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE=1 without per-experiment gating overhead; the dry session can skip GPU health checks entirely.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: Top contributors: DualGPURunner parallelism on dual-model experiments (~8%), inference batching (~6%), doc-only test-skip classifier (~4%), conductor health check at session start preventing env-propagation blocks (~5%), partial-result fast-path on interruptions (~4%), deduplication of re-verification turns (~5%). Combined estimated reduction: approximately 32% of total wall time, bringing a comparable 311-experiment milestone from 5002 min to approximately 3400 min.
